match.reason: The bank card covers the multiplication principle but also teaches the addition principle and combined problems, and it comes from a Units 1 and 2 senior course, so it is broader and at a different depth from this Year 10 point.

draft.title: The multiplication principle
card: When you make one choice and then another, multiply the number of ways. If the first choice can be made in \(m\) ways and the second in \(n\) ways, there are \(m \times n\) ways altogether.
Example: 3 shirts and 4 pairs of pants give \(3 \times 4 = 12\) outfits. Each shirt can go with any of the 4 pants.
It works for more than two choices too. Multiply the number of ways for each choice. Adding 5 hats to the outfit gives \(3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60\) outfits.
Do not add the numbers. Adding would count the shirts and pants as separate things, but an outfit uses one of each.
draft.remember: Choices made one after another: multiply the number of ways for each.

a.q: Mia picks one of 5 sandwiches and one of 3 drinks for lunch. How many different lunches can she make?
a.why: Each of the 5 sandwiches can go with any of the 3 drinks, so there are \(5 \times 3 = 15\) lunches. Adding to get 8 is tempting, but a lunch uses one of each, so the numbers must be multiplied.
a.clue: Each sandwich can be paired with every drink.

b.q: A café in Dubbo offers 4 soups, 3 mains and 2 desserts. A meal is one soup, one main and one dessert. How many different meals are possible?
b.why: There are three choices in a row, so multiply: \(4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24\). Multiplying only the first two choices gives 12, but the dessert choice also multiplies the number of meals.
b.clue: There are three choices, so use all three numbers.
